recommendedFormats.interactiveVectors: GeoJSON in WGS84 for dated polity areas, boundary lines, place points, popups and feature styling; simplify prepared display copies only.
recommendedFormats.largeVectorDelivery: TopoJSON can reduce shared boundary duplication; vector tiles/PMTiles become useful if the map later loads many dates or detailed local layers.
recommendedFormats.historicalPaperMaps: Keep a georeferenced GeoTIFF master; publish tiled raster/XYZ or a georeferenced image overlay. An archival JPG/JP2 needs georeferencing before geographic overlay; an IIIF viewer alone is not a geospatial registration.

source.title: Cliopatria
source.credit: Historical polity reconstruction: Cliopatria, Seshat Global History Databank, CC BY 4.0. Cropped to the map region.

filter: Type == 'POLITY' and FromYear <= snapshotYear <= ToYear; BCE years negative, CE positive. No interpolation or movement of borders between source records.
changes: Original archive and original GeoJSON preserved unmodified.
Each dated snapshot clipped to [20, 20, 55, 45] in WGS84, topology-preserving simplified by 0.01 degrees, snapped to a 0.00001-degree grid and rounded to five decimals.

Source properties preserved verbatim, including FromYear, ToYear and Area; labelLon/labelLat added from a representative point of the largest clipped polygon part. Area remains the SOURCE FULL POLITY area, not clipped area.
Source has no feature IDs; GeoJSON id and sourceFeatureIndex preserve its zero-based record index, keyed by source SHA-256.
Invalid source geometry repaired only where needed; line/point artifacts discarded from polygon output; all final geometry valid and every label anchor verified covered by its polygon.

displayBoundary preserves the original polygon boundary intersected with the map extent and simplified by 0.01 degrees. The viewer strokes this separate geometry so clipping edges are not presented as historical borders.
sourceLimitations: A scholarly broad-scale reconstruction, not precise administrative mapping; source does not encode boundary uncertainty or competing territorial claims.
Year filtering selects a source interval, not evidence of an independent survey for every year.
Ancient Canaan and Temple-period categories are interpretive headings; displayed snapshots retain the exact selected year and individual source polity names.
No detailed Canaan city-state, First Temple local-border, Byzantine provincial or Ottoman district geometry was verified during this bounded task.
Source polity names can persist across regimes: chronological name review is required before treating every Name as a contemporary political designation. Flagged examples are included below.
Aggregate and component polity records can overlap; parenthesized source names and Components/MemberOf fields must not be mistaken for mutually exclusive territorial partitions.

Historical outlines are generalized and can differ from the modern coastline. They must not be used to infer territorial membership of an individual reference pin. Period groups do not date every reference or imply that all places were inhabited in the selected year.

periods.title: Ancient Canaan
periods.scopeNote: Broad regional polities around Canaan; not a single Canaan boundary or a complete city-state map.

periods.title: First Temple period
periods.scopeNote: One snapshot during the First Temple period; not boundaries for the entire period.

periods.title: Second Temple period
periods.scopeNote: Late Second Temple snapshot. Imperial territory does not supply Judean internal administrative borders.

periods.title: Byzantine period
periods.scopeNote: Byzantine-era territorial context for this year, not a map of church dioceses or all Byzantine centuries.

periods.title: Ottoman period
periods.scopeNote: Empire-level context in 1600, not Ottoman provincial or district boundaries.

periods.title: Before World War I
polityNames: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia
periods.scopeNote: Annual territorial reconstruction for 1913, not an exact-day diplomatic or administrative map.

periods.title: Modern
periods.scopeNote: Existing modern reference layer retains source dispute classifications. Its release is not a real-time border survey.

alternatives.title: CShapes 2.0
alternatives.note: Useful pre-WWI state/territory boundaries; noncommercial restriction differs from the R package's software license. Not downloaded here.

alternatives.title: Edward Stanford 1912 map, Constantinople to Calcutta
alternatives.institution: Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division
alternatives.licenseNote: LOC item says free to use and reuse unless an overriding rights advisory is present; none observed.
alternatives.semantics: Historical paper map showing international boundaries, communications and spheres of influence.
alternatives.formatRecommendation: Georeference the downloadable raster, retain a GeoTIFF master and serve tiles; do not silently treat image pixel coordinates as geographic coordinates.

displayPolicy: Source names and date intervals remain verbatim in downloads. Map labels show biblical/present-day site names, not unchecked regime labels from source Name fields. Every reference pin remains available independently of the period layer.
